- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < -0.3) — model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.  
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model often follows sentiment too aggressively, leading to overcorrection or premature reversal.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect from recent highs/lows, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too optimistic in early part of the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile.  
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often fails to account for diminishing momentum — underestimates peak and then overcorrects later.  
- Model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is mildly negative but price is still trending up — fails to recognize early reversal signals.
